title: Congruent and Similar Triangles
seo_title: Year 10 Maths: Congruent and Similar Triangles Worksheets (GCSE)
standard_text: Use the basic congruence criteria for triangles (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS); apply the concepts of congruence and similarity, including the relationships between lengths.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE maths worksheets on congruence conditions SSS, SAS, AAS and RHS and finding lengths in similar triangles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Congruent: same shape and size (SSS, SAS, AAS, RHS). Similar: same shape (AA, SSS, SAS).
key_sub: Match the letters in order to find corresponding sides and angles.
body_html:
How it works

Congruent triangles are exactly the same shape and size. Tests: SSS, SAS (the angle must be between the sides), AAS and RHS (right angle, hypotenuse, side). AAA does not prove congruence.

Similar triangles are the same shape: corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio. Tests: AA (two pairs of equal angles), SSS (all three ratios equal) and SAS (two ratios equal and the included angle equal).

Write the letters in matching order: in △ABC ≡ △PQR, A matches P, B matches Q and C matches R.

Example

In △ABC, DE ∥ BC, AD = 4 cm, DB = 2 cm and DE = 6 cm. Find BC.

△ADE and △ABC are similar (AA)

AB = 6 cm, so the scale factor is 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5

Answer: BC = 9 cm

Example

△ABC has sides 6, 8, 10. △PQR has sides 9, 12, 15. Are they similar?

9 ÷ 6 = 12 ÷ 8 = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5

Answer: Yes, by SSS similarity

Common mistakes

  • Thinking three equal angles (AAA) prove two triangles are congruent.
  • Using SAS when the angle is not between the two sides.
  • Matching the wrong sides. Match shortest to shortest and longest to longest.
  • Using DB instead of the whole side AB when DE ∥ BC.

faq.q: What are the tests for congruent triangles?
faq.a: SSS (three sides), SAS (two sides and the included angle), AAS (two angles and a corresponding side) and RHS (right angle, hypotenuse and one other side).

faq.q: What are the tests for similar triangles?
faq.a: AA (two pairs of equal angles), SSS (all three pairs of sides in the same ratio) and SAS (two pairs of sides in the same ratio with the included angles equal).

faq.q: What is the difference between congruent and similar?
faq.a: Congruent triangles are the same shape and the same size. Similar triangles are the same shape but can be different sizes.

faq.q: Why does the order of letters matter?
faq.a: △ABC ≡ △PQR tells you A matches P, B matches Q and C matches R, so you can find corresponding sides and angles.

items.q: Jack is 1.7 m tall and casts a shadow 2.5 m long. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow 10 m long. How tall is the tree?
items.e: The sun's rays make similar triangles, so height ÷ shadow is the same: 1.7 ÷ 2.5 = h ÷ 10, h = 6.8 m.

items.q: △ABC ≡ △PQR. ∠A = 36° and ∠B = 33°. Find ∠R.
items.e: The letters match in order: ∠R matches ∠C. ∠C = 180° − 36° − 33° = 111°, so ∠R = 111°.

items.q: In △ABC, DE is parallel to BC, with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 3 cm, DB = 4 cm and DE = 3 cm. Find BC.
